layers.note: An invasive shrub of dry, open, disturbed ground: prairies, clearings and road edges.

heat_load.note: Warm, sunny ground; favours slopes facing south and west.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 800 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Grows on flats and moderate slopes.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −2 °C, gone by −6 °C, up to about 13 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −18 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −26 °C.

warmest_c.note: Warmest-month means from about 13 to 25 °C, gone below 10 °C and above 29 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 2,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,400.

degree_days_5.note: About 900 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 500.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.35, gone by 0.25.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; naturalised under summer-dry and summer-wet temperate climates to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Scotch broom, from western Europe, is naturalised on the Pacific coast and in other mild climates; hard winters kill it back (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
